paper.title_en: Characterizing the Thermal Quantum Correlations in a Two-Qubit Heisenberg XYZ Spin-1/2 Chain Under an External Magnetic Field with Spin-Orbit and Zeeman Interactions
paper.abstract_en: We present a comprehensive theoretical study of thermal quantum correlations in a two-qubit Heisenberg XYZ spin-1/2 chain under the combined influence of an external magnetic field, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) antisymmetric and Kaplan-Shekhtman-Entin-Wohlman-Aharony (KSEA) symmetric spin-orbit interactions, and Zeeman splitting. We derive closed-form analytical expressions for two complementary discord-type quantifiers - the trace distance discord (TDD) and the local quantum uncertainty (LQU) - as functions of temperature, magnetic field, spin-orbit coupling parameters, and Zeeman energy. Our analysis reveals that the DM interaction provides robust thermal protection for quantum correlations, while the KSEA interaction produces asymmetric effects on the two correlation measures. The magnetic field and Zeeman interaction offer effective control knobs for modulating correlations, exhibiting non-monotonic behavior that arises from the competition between Zeeman polarization and exchange interactions. We extend our analysis to both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic exchange regimes, demonstrating that the qualitative behavior of quantum correlations is preserved across both phases. Finally, we connect our theoretical findings to realistic solid-state platforms, including semiconductor quantum dots and molecular magnets, providing experimental benchmarks for current quantum information technologies.
